pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (associated with an Ovarian Teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: The combination of psychiatric prodrome, characteristic orofacial dyskinesias, extreme delta brush pattern on EEG, autonomic instability, and an underlying mature cystic ovarian teratoma. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ectopic neural tissue within an ovarian teratoma (or triggered by viral prodrome) expresses the GluN1/NR1 subunit of NMDA receptors, triggering a systemic autoimmune response. Cross-reactive autoantibodies (IgG against GluN1) cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to NMDA receptors on GABAergic interneurons in the forebrain, causing cross-linking, antibody-mediated receptor internalization, and profound NMDA-pathway hypofunction. This loss of inhibitory control results in excess glutamate/dopamine release, manifesting sequentially as psychosis, catatonia, stereotyped orofacial movement disorders, autonomic collapse, and central respiratory failure. Treatment requires tumor resection and aggressive immunotherapy (corticosteroids, IVIG/plasma exchange, and rituximab).
